FROMLIST: ath10k: fix group privacy action frame decryption for qca4019 Recent commit 'mac80211: Encrypt "Group addressed privacy" action frames' encrypts group privacy action frames. But qca99x0 family chipset delivers broadcast/multicast management frames as encrypted and it should be decrypted by mac80211. Setting RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED stats for those frames is breaking mesh connection establishment. (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/9270363/) BUG=chrome-os-partner:55285 TEST=built ath10k modules for x86 Change-Id: I3a93d5523c7c8808141a848d524a083a038d885b Signed-off-by: Rajkumar Manoharan <rmanohar@qti.qualcomm.com> Signed-off-by: Tamizh chelvam <c_traja@qti.qualcomm.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/367023 Commit-Ready: Julan Hsu <julanhsu@google.com> Tested-by: Julan Hsu <julanhsu@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

cryptohome: Extract attestation into dbus service child class To prepare for implementing a version of cryptohome dbus service that bounces attestation-related calls to attestationd, extract attestation-related functionality into a separate class dependant on Service and make attestation-related methods abstract in the base Service. This approach was chosen over extracting it into a separate class that can be instantiated by Service depending on the chosen attestation implementation for the following reasons: To minimize changes to the existing code, attestation methods continue to rely on Service's internal objects: mount_thread, event_source, etc. They also occasionally use tpm, tpm_init and other such objects, pointers to which are handled by Service. Giving access to it for dependant classes is more natural and less intrusive than exposing all needed internal objects to an independant class. Thus, after the two approaches (inheritance vs object encapsulation) were implemented and compared, inheritance had a more concise code and required less changes to the code that uses Service: interface, cryptohomed, unittests. BUG=chrome-os-partner:54712 TEST=cryptohome unittests cryptohome --action=tpm_attestation_status cryptohome --action=tpm_more_status login_Cryptohome platform_Attestation (TPM1.2 only) Change-Id: I205bbd4f03e737281f3d27c790cea076205818e6 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/368890 Commit-Ready: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Tested-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Darren Krahn <dkrahn@chromium.org>

minigbm: Add userspace reference counting When a dmabuf is imported multiple times, further imports after the first one are not refcounted, i.e. the first close() will lose the dmabuf. To avoid this, user space needs to track the number of imports and only close() the dmabuf once the last import is closed. BUG=None TEST=Ran graphics_Gbm on minnie. Still passes. CHROMIUM: mesh: put path add/del debugfs tasks in workqueue mesh path add/del can happen in thread or softirq contexts, and some while holding rcu locks. This is problematic to debugfs operations which can sleep. Create a queue for all debugfs add/del tasks, and path add/del routines will just queue the debugfs tasks and send a signal. The actual debugfs operations are performed in mac80211 workqueue. Also add a spinlock to synchronize the queue access. BUG=b:29076511 TEST=2-node gale mesh. Reboot the mesh point 50 times and verify no backtraces are seen. Same tests on whirlwind mesh. Change-Id: Ib559a6f3f586e90e836b0eb1bd7173be8ea25ea0 Signed-off-by: Julan Hsu <julanhsu@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/351232 Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/366755
